description: Split the Epics list Active bucket into four presentation groups (Running / Ready to start / Waiting-Blocked / Idle-Empty) computed from the existing Epic read model, render group-aware cards with a clarified Start next issue action, and keep the page mobile-overflow-free. Frontend-only.

tasks.title: Implement groupActiveEpics cascade selector with unit tests
tasks.description: Add a pure `groupActiveEpics(epics: EpicWithProgress[])` selector (sibling to EpicListPage, e.g. groupActiveEpics.ts) that buckets active (idle/running) epics into running / readyToStart / waitingBlocked / idleEmpty by first-match cascade over progress.activeIssues, progress.nextIssue, progress.nextIssueReason. Ship it with dedicated unit tests covering each bucket and the active-issue-beats-nextIssueReason precedence invariant. The selector must rely solely on existing list read-model fields and must not invoke the epic detail-enrichment path.
acceptanceCriteria: Selector returns four disjoint buckets and every active epic lands in exactly one bucket (no epic appears in two buckets, no active epic is dropped).
Epic with non-empty progress.activeIssues is placed in running, even when progress.nextIssueReason is also non-null (active-issue check wins the cascade).
Epic with no active issue and non-null progress.nextIssue is placed in readyToStart.
Epic with no active issue, null progress.nextIssue, and non-null progress.nextIssueReason is placed in waitingBlocked.
Epic with no active issue, null nextIssue, and null nextIssueReason is placed in idleEmpty.
Selector is pure, depends only on EpicWithProgress.progress fields, and does not call into LinkedIssue.canStart or any detail-enrichment path.
`npm run typecheck -w packages/web` passes and the selector unit tests pass via `npm run test:run -w packages/web`.
tasks.output: packages/web/src/pages/epics/ui/groupActiveEpics.ts (+ groupActiveEpics.test.ts) ready to be consumed by EpicListPage
tasks.notes: Design D1 (pure cascade selector) and D2 (group on nextIssue presence, not CanStart). Independent unit-testable foundation for T-002.

tasks.title: Refactor EpicListPage into four active groups with group-aware cards and mobile-safe layout
tasks.description: Consume groupActiveEpics in EpicListPage and render six EpicSections in fixed order (Running, Ready to start, Waiting/Blocked, Idle/Empty expanded by default; Done and Closed folded; Paused left inline). Make EpicCard group-aware: Running shows the in-progress issue number+title; Ready to start shows the next issue number+title plus a control labelled exactly `Start next issue`; Waiting/Blocked shows nextIssueReason; Idle/Empty shows `Ready to mark done` or an explicit empty-state message. Gate `Start next issue` to Ready-to-start cards only (remove the unconditional Start button). Enforce mobile no-overflow structurally (wrap + flexible widths, no fixed/min-width on state-bearing elements). Rewrite EpicListPage.test.tsx to the new groups, ordering, card content, Start gating, Done/Closed folded behavior, and the stubbed no-overflow assertion at 320/390/430px.
acceptanceCriteria: Active groups render top-to-bottom in the order Running, Ready to start, Waiting/Blocked, Idle/Empty; a Running epic appears above a Ready-to-start epic.

Section test-ids are epic-section-running, epic-section-ready, epic-section-waiting, epic-section-idle; the legacy epic-section-active is removed; epic-section-done and epic-section-closed are retained.
The four active groups are expanded by default (toggle aria-expanded='true' on load); Done and Closed are folded (aria-expanded='false') and their cards are not visible until expanded.
A Running card displays the current in-progress issue number and title and offers NO Start next issue control.

A Ready-to-start card displays the next issue number and title and a manual control labelled exactly `Start next issue` (not `Start`, not `Start Epic`); invoking it starts only that next issue and performs no epic lifecycle Start Epic transition.

Waiting/Blocked cards display progress.nextIssueReason; Idle/Empty cards display `Ready to mark done` when progress.readyToMarkDone is true, otherwise an explicit empty-state message (e.g. `No linked issues`); neither offers a Start next issue control.

No fixed-width or min-width is applied to status/priority badges, the progress bar, current/next/reason text, or the Start next issue control; state-bearing strings (status badge + current/next issue number) are not truncated and remain visible; long titles/reasons wrap via break-words/line-clamp/flex-wrap.

With epics present across all four active groups and documentElement.scrollWidth/clientWidth stubbed equal at 320px, 390px, and 430px, the rendered page asserts documentElement.scrollWidth <= documentElement.clientWidth at every width.
`npm run typecheck -w packages/web` and `npm run test:run -w packages/web` both pass.
